## Audit item 25 measured — NOT a simple deletion
Dropping the `runtime-dispatch-common`/`runtime-delegation` slots from `templates/routing/compact-recovery.skeleton.md` regenerates cleanly (24 surfaces) but reds: test-issue-1044-prompt-bundle (A1/B1/B2), test-issue-1044-runtime-adapters (B1 Cursor), grok-edition G5, cursor-edition G2/G5 — all state that for Grok and Cursor the global-transaction Rule rendered from the recovery skeleton is the ALWAYS-LOADED carrier of the dispatch contract and runtime adapter (there is no other carrier on those hosts). So the duplication exists only where a runtime's full Next/Finalize reload carries dispatch again (claude, codex, and the additive command editions); for the Rule-carrier runtimes the block is load-bearing. The skeleton edit was reverted; the per-runtime resolution (omit the blocks only in recovery renders whose runtime reloads a full surface carrying them) is handed to the implementer with the acceptance author pinning it per runtime. Evidence: this file; commands in the orchestrator transcript (edition lane run at the time of measurement).

## Shared-boundary carrier decision (audit item 10, grounded in `.cache/runtime-inheritance.md`)
Measured: claude/opencode/grok subagents inherit the global contract and AGENTS.md; kimi subagents see only the role body + runtime-adapter appendix; cursor subagents on CLI build 2026.09.02-c22c1a3 inherit project but not the global contract (the primary misses it too — host-side, out of scope); codex unknown (spawn output undecodable 4/4); zcode not run.
Measured on the bodies: neither the pre-#1054 bodies nor the rewritten ones ever carried the global contract's shared boundaries (0 of 14 old/new bodies mention unexecuted-check claims, First Principles, the Mission List, the global contract, or AGENTS.md). The rewrite therefore removed no shared-boundary sentence that a non-inheriting host used to deliver; nothing is restored.
Decision: role bodies carry positioning, deliverable, unique custody, and stop; shared boundaries stay in the machine-global contract and AGENTS.md; the evidence-honesty boundary reaches every host through the deliverable itself ("the checks you ran … and what you did not run"). No new adapter field, appendix block, or body sentence is added for kimi: an added mechanism would be speculative for the six other hosts and would not be a measured capability of kimi's schema. The kimi/cursor/codex facts are reported to the user in the run record as host observations; the cursor global-contract miss and the missing Kaola subagent_type enum on that build are out of #1054 scope and are not filed automatically.

## Native behavior acceptance (mission 14) — regression found and repaired
inherit-1054's first pass (`.cache/native-behavior.md`): claude 10/10 correct old and new (new is compact, old reproduced its retired output template); opencode and kimi fail the fixed-destination routing probe under BOTH bodies (standing gap, not a regression); grok and codex OLD declined the probe, grok and codex NEW invented a metric and hardcoded the destination (verified on disk) — a real regression: the rewritten body's single sentence "belongs to the implementer" was not enough where the old body's ratchet section had said it twice with an explicit "never invent a kind". cursor unknown (no role override on this build), zcode unknown (no binary).
Repair in the authority (metric-optimizer, custody + stop): before any change confirm the brief names a measurable metric and a direction; a fixed destination (make X true / make this test pass / return this value) is the implementer's work — stop without touching a file, say so, do not invent a metric to stand in for it; "Stop before starting when the brief has no metric". Regenerated 126 renders; role-redesign 193, generation checks and validate-vendored-agents green. Re-measurement of task 5 on every executed host is dispatched to inherit-1054; the run is not closed until that table exists.
